power_constraint_analysis: Both configurations are rated at 60 MW, exceeding the 50 MW requirement by 10 MW. Power is not the limiting factor in either case.
final_answer: The baseline is partially feasible: its 60 MW rating exceeds the 50 MW need, but its 180 MWh capacity and 3-hour duration fall short of the 200 MWh, 4-hour event. With power unchanged at 60 MW and energy increased to 240 MWh, the counterfactual configuration meets the stated power, energy, and duration requirements.
scenario_impact: Increasing energy capacity without changing power preserves the ability to meet the event's instantaneous power demand while extending support from 3 to 4 hours. The change makes the specified 4-hour grid support event feasible.
source_question: A grid support event requires 50 MW continuously for 4 hours, or 200 MWh. The baseline system is rated at 60 MW with 180 MWh of usable energy and a 3-hour rated discharge duration. If usable energy is increased to 240 MWh while power remains unchanged, does the revised system meet the event, and what limitation applies to the baseline?
energy_duration_constraint_analysis: The baseline has 180 MWh against a 200 MWh requirement and a 3-hour rated duration against 4 hours, so it cannot sustain the full event. The revised configuration has 240 MWh and a 4-hour rated duration, meeting both the energy and duration requirements.
